headline: Healthy Food Doesn't Have to Taste Like Punishment
deck: Changing the nutrition profile does not mean giving up seasoning, texture, contrast or the reason people wanted to eat the dish in the first place.
author: Josh Freeman
heroImageAlt: Chef and team preparing organized meal service
body: A lot of healthier food fails because the cook removes fat, salt or sugar and forgets to replace the job those ingredients were doing.

Flavor can come from browning, acids, aromatics, herbs, spice, roasted vegetables and better texture. Satisfaction also matters. If people do not want to eat the meal, the nutrition numbers on paper are not doing much good.
Health-oriented cooking works better when the goal is a better dish with smarter choices, not a punishment version of the original.
joshTake: My first question is always: will somebody actually want a second bite? If the answer is no, I am not done just because the nutrition panel looks nicer.
seoTitle: Healthy Food Does Not Have to Taste Like Punishment
seoDescription: Practical ways to improve healthier food using browning, acid, aromatics, texture and smarter cooking rather than simply removing flavor.
